review_note: Checked: helper and test read line by line; test and helper SHA-256 match the receipt; the 3 linked row_keys equal the 3 receipt candidate_rows verbatim. Oracle: b34_gaussian_marginal() is base R (dense V = sigma^2 I + (sd %o% sd)*K indexed by level, Cholesky), with a hand Henderson tabular A (40 animals, diagonal 1.25 for full-sib offspring, asserted), a hand relmat K (diagonal 0.49 to 2.56, asserted non-unit) and a hand exp(-d/median)+1e-6 kernel; no drmTMB code. It is evaluated at the live Julia estimates (engine='julia', Julia 1.10.0, 3 live blocks ran, skips 0). Agreement with logLik(fit): relmat 2.8e-13, animal 5.7e-14, spatial 5.7e-14 (tolerance 1e-8). Each fit is intercept-only SD (sd(id, level=...) ~ z), q=1, independent, so no correlation is required; the rows are fitted literally. Emulated bugs are asserted above 20 x tol: selectors swapped 95/380/119, reversed SD vector 4.7/29.8/12.7, kernel read by position 83/10.3/10.0, SD intercept +log 2 9.5/9.0/9.5, cov2cor(K) 1.00 (relmat) and 0.25 (animal), mean-distance range 0.0465 (spatial, the smallest gap, 4.6 million times tol). Rows shuffled, levels named, kernel/coordinates supplied in a different order and the fit asserts the unique(id) order differs from the levels. A one-step profile check at +-0.1 on every mu and SD coefficient stays below the oracle maximum. Console log clean (0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips, 0 warnings; only the experimental-engine notice and Julia startup lines). What this does NOT establish: one fixture and one seed per route; no calibration, coverage, SE or Hessian parity, or recovery. The hand spatial kernel (median positive distance, 1e-6 jitter) is rebuilt to match the package convention, so agreement confirms the convention is implemented as written, not that it is the right one. The animal fit supplies A as a matrix, so pedigree to A construction in the package is not tested. sigma is not profile-checked. fitted() and residuals() are not covered. The test does not assert that the fit object records engine 'julia' (the Julia notice and live-block count in the log show it ran).
